copy_gate.detail: the gating file matches the pattern

why: the file is the owner's own configuration or log; its text is kept, with user profile folder names, e-mail shaped tokens, UNC host names and hardware addresses replaced by pseudonyms (see protection)

protection.user_pseudonym: user-<first 12 hex of SHA-256(salt, name)>, every folder name after \Users\ in a path, except the standard folders Public, Default, Default User and All Users
protection.mail_pseudonym: mail-<first 12 hex of SHA-256(salt, address)>, every e-mail shaped token
protection.host_pseudonym: host-<first 12 hex of SHA-256(salt, name)>, the host of every UNC path (two leading separators)
protection.mac_pseudonym: mac-<first 12 hex of SHA-256(salt, address)>, every six pair hardware address
protection.limits: a DOMAIN\\user pair, an account name outside a path, or a computer name standing alone has no shape of its own and is not caught
protection.salt: random per run, never written; pseudonyms are consistent inside this bundle only
protection.encoding: the copy is UTF-8 without a byte order mark; the source encoding is recorded in result.json
protection.argument_removal: on every line, everything after the first program (the first .exe, .com, .bat or .cmd, in any case, directly followed by a double quote, white space, a comma or the end of the line; the closing quote is kept when one directly follows) is replaced by <arguments omitted>, whatever the vendor switch said when the line was written; columns after the program are lost with it; the copy gate is a second layer (see copy_gate)
protection.argument_removal_limits: a logged command whose program has none of those extensions is not caught; read the copy before the bundle leaves the PC

sharing: the file is opened for reading with writers allowed to continue; a file being appended may be read mid line, and the hash is of the bytes read
